assets.statement: L1-as-branch-B-evidence fails: Maynard bound is subsequence-only (hidden-subsequence attack) and does not match the quantifier reversal of o(log N) (needs all-N failure at positive density, not infinitely many N); repair = uniform c·log N lower bound on the full primes, an equivalent-strength open p

L1 = "record bounds 5≤min s≤10^7 close Branch A" fails: minimal case k=5 — no ∀-side obstruction for min s specifically, quantifier slip confirmed, and the route continues only by renaming the difficulty (§4.1 circularity); repair = explicit m with colouring witness s≤m plus universal (m−1)-term blu

k=1 case does not transfer: iterating gives F(N+k)≤F(N)+k not +1; no rigidity lemma or branch-B witness supplied; closer refusal upheld; repair needs either structural rigidity of maximal Sidon extensions (KSS obstruction on record from erdos44 R002/L1) or explicit infinite family with F(N+k)≥F(N)+2

REFUTED by external audit (GPT gold-mine audit + R4, 2026-09-01), each item re-verified by the operator's session against the frozen contract or by exact computation on 2026-09-02 | FALSE: Pintz/Rankin-type results concern LARGE GAPS between consecutive primes, not the length of arithmetic progressions of primes in [1,N]. No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.

exact integer enumeration over odd n in [3,15] shows rule "n−2 composite or n−2≤1" yields A={3,11} not {1,3}; asserted member 1 is outside the stated domain, so the lemma as stated is false — intended rule must be resupplied.

circular/ equivalent-strength: "new primes must eventually appear" restates F(n)→∞; additionally quantifier slip — limit clause does not imply F(n)>n ∀ sufficiently large n; both contract clauses remain open, no candidate lemma was supplied beyond the tautology.
